cases.name: wide
cases.when: responsive is false, or the container is at least --bp-md -- the default shape, a real role="grid" the arrow keys walk

cases.name: card
cases.when: responsive is true and the container is below --bp-md -- one card per row, no grid, row or cell role anywhere
cases.reason: Below the breakpoint there is no grid: the rows become stacked cards and nothing carries a grid, row or cell role. The grid pattern's requirements do not go unmet in this shape, they do not APPLY to it -- there is no grid for a roving tab stop to live in. The sort control this shape draws instead is a Select, which carries Select's own binding and not a clause of this one, and it is what keeps a sortable column reachable where there is no header row to activate. Whether a card a consumer made clickable is reachable by keyboard is TableRow's question, not a clause of this one, and that binding records where this layer stands on it.

cases.name: empty
cases.when: no TableRow is written -- the [empty] slot alone, with no grid drawn at all
cases.reason: There is no grid in this shape, so the grid pattern's requirements do not go unmet, they do not APPLY. A role="grid" holding neither a header row nor a data row is a degenerate render, the same judgement Tabs makes when it draws no tabpanel for a tab that does not exist, and a column head standing over a "no results" sentence describes a table that is not there. The measurement that settled it: across sixteen tables in a real consumer the slot had zero uses and was replaced every time by an @if that removed the table entirely.
